questions.concept: Workpool zero parallelism pauses queued work
questions.context:
Convex 1.41.0 and Workpool 0.4.8. recordEvent inserts an event and enqueues its statistics update through one mounted Workpool. Only these queued mutations write statistics. A developer tries to serialize the updates with this setting:

```ts
const statsPool = new Workpool(components.workpool, { maxParallelism: 0 });
```

Three events are committed. No jobs were running before them, and the pool configuration stays unchanged.
questions.question: What happens to the queued statistics updates?

options.text: They stay queued; none starts until the pool permits work.
options.rationale: Zero pauses new work. A control that sets the mounted pool to one drains all three jobs.

options.text: They run one at a time, because zero disables parallel execution.
options.rationale: Serialization requires a positive limit of one; zero permits no new worker.

options.text: They are discarded, because a zero-capacity pool cannot accept work.
options.rationale: Enqueue still records durable jobs. Raising the limit later runs the previously queued updates.

options.text: One runs and the remaining two wait, because zero means no extra workers.
options.rationale: The setting counts the total allowed running work, not workers beyond an implicit first one.
